roles.name: policyholder
roles.title: Driver
roles.description: One of the two drivers. Holds a policy with their own insurer, knows what happened as they saw it, and holds whatever evidence they have. Can report the loss, give a statement, hand over documents, have the car repaired, rent a car, pay bills, and accept or reject an offer.

roles.name: adjuster
roles.title: Claims adjuster
roles.description: Handles every claim made on one insurer for this accident: by its own insured under the policy, and by the other driver against its insured. Verifies coverage, gathers evidence, decides fault, pays, and settles with the other insurer.

actions.name: search_handbook
actions.summary: Search the policy form, the claims rules, the liability guide and the forum's rules.
actions.description: A driver gets the policy form and the guide for claimants. An adjuster gets those and the insurer's claims manual.

actions.name: list_claims
actions.summary: List the claims this seat is a party to or handles.

actions.name: get_claim
actions.summary: Read a claim.

actions.name: get_document
actions.summary: Read a document this seat holds a copy of.

actions.name: list_my_documents
actions.summary: List the documents this seat holds a copy of.

actions.name: get_my_policy
actions.summary: Read the declarations of one's own policy.

actions.name: get_my_account
actions.summary: What the driver has paid, received and still owes.

actions.name: report_claim
actions.summary: Report the accident to one's own insurer, or claim against the other driver's.
actions.description: Reported to one's own insurer, it opens the coverages of one's own policy that are asked for. Made against the other driver's insurer, it opens a claim for the damage that driver is responsible for. Both can be done.

actions.name: give_statement
actions.summary: Answer an adjuster's request for a statement about the accident.

actions.name: submit_document
actions.summary: Give a claim a copy of a document one holds.

actions.name: request_estimate
actions.summary: Ask one's repair shop for a written estimate.

actions.name: get_repair_status
actions.summary: Where the repair of one's car stands.

actions.name: authorize_repair
actions.summary: Tell the shop to go ahead. The owner owes the shop its bill.

actions.name: rent_car
actions.summary: Rent a car. It costs the daily rate until it is returned.

actions.name: return_car
actions.summary: Return the rental car. The rental company bills the days used.

actions.name: pay_bill
actions.summary: Pay a bill of the repair shop, the rental company or the towing company.

actions.name: respond_to_offer
actions.summary: Accept or reject an insurer's offer.
actions.description: Accepting settles the amounts the offer names with that insurer. Accepting an offer for the vehicle or its towing closes one's own collision coverage for them: the vehicle is settled one way. Rejecting leaves the items open.

actions.name: get_policy
actions.summary: Read a policy of one's own insurer: period, cancellation, coverages.

actions.name: acknowledge_claim
actions.summary: Acknowledge a claimant's notice in writing and say how to go on.

actions.name: request_information
actions.summary: Ask a driver for a statement, for documents, or both.

actions.name: request_police_report
actions.summary: Order the police report of the accident.

actions.name: contact_witness
actions.summary: Ask a witness named in the file for a statement.

actions.name: order_appraisal
actions.summary: Have the insurer's appraiser review an estimate or a supplement.
actions.description: The report says for each line whether the damage comes from this accident.

actions.name: decide_exposure
actions.summary: Accept or deny an exposure. A denial is sent to the claimant in writing, with its reasons.

actions.name: decide_liability
actions.summary: Record the insurer's determination of each driver's share of the fault.
actions.description: Every determination is kept. The last one stands, and an offer is made at the share it gives the insured.

actions.name: make_offer
actions.summary: Offer the other driver a settlement of items of their claim against the insured.
actions.description: Needs a determination of fault on record that puts a share on the insured; the offer carries that share and the kinds of evidence the determination names. The vehicle and its towing are settled one way: a claimant who has claimed them under their own collision coverage gets them there, and the two insurers settle between themselves. Rental can be owed by both: by the claimant's own policy within its limits, and by the insured for the rest. A new offer withdraws an open one on the same exposure.

actions.name: issue_payment
actions.summary: Pay on an exposure.
actions.description: To one's own insured under a coverage (`coverage`), or their share of a recovery (`deductible_reimbursement`, on the collision exposure, as the item `deductible`). To the other driver on an accepted offer (`liability`). To the other insurer on an agreed demand (`subrogation`) or an award (`award`), on the exposure of the driver the demand is for; the deductible in the demand may be named as the item `deductible`.

actions.name: send_letter
actions.summary: Send a driver a written status, an excess notice, a notice about recovery, or a closing letter.
actions.description: A status letter is about one exposure, goes to its claimant, and names what is still needed before a decision.

actions.name: send_demand
actions.summary: Demand from the other insurer what was paid to one's own insured, deductible included.
actions.description: One demand is made for one accident, and nothing can be added to it later: send it when everything you will pay your insured has been paid. The documents sent with it go on the other insurer's file. Each item demanded needs a document that shows its amount: an appraisal, an estimate or a repair invoice for the vehicle, the rental invoice, the towing invoice.

actions.name: respond_to_demand
actions.summary: Accept what is on the table, counter with another share or other amounts, or deny.
actions.description: A counter names a share of fault and may name the amounts it accepts, by item, and the deductible. Accepting takes the share and the amounts of the other insurer's last turn.

actions.name: file_arbitration
actions.summary: Put one's own demand, which the two insurers cannot settle, before the forum.
actions.description: Only the insurer that made the demand can file it.

actions.name: answer_arbitration
actions.summary: Put one's own evidence and contention before the forum.

actions.name: get_arbitration
actions.summary: Read an arbitration case.

actions.name: close_claim
actions.summary: Close a claim on which nothing is left undecided.
actions.description: A closed claim takes no further decisions, offers or payments. A new notice or a demand reopens it.

actions.name: send_message
actions.summary: Send a message to one or more seats.
actions.description: Free text plus typed attachments. To make an offer, create the world object first and attach a reference to it; a price written in text commits nobody.

actions.name: read_inbox
actions.summary: Read unread messages, optionally waiting for the next one.
actions.description: With `wait_minutes` the world clock advances while the seat sleeps. The wait ends early when a message or an event notice for this seat arrives, and it never runs past the end of the observation period.

actions.name: get_message_history
actions.summary: Page through earlier messages of this seat.

actions.name: finish
actions.summary: Hand back control and end this seat's session.
actions.description: Finishing does not stop the world. Pending holds, deadlines and scheduled events still settle until the task's observation end, with nobody acting for this seat.

manners.name: by the book
manners.does: Does what the claims manual says.

manners.name: low first offer
manners.does: Its first offer to the other driver is 70 percent of what it finds owed. After a rejection it offers the whole.

manners.name: never concedes
manners.does: Answers every demand with half the share of fault its file gives, and lets the forum decide.

manners.name: own word
manners.does: Decides fault on its own insured's statement and asks nobody else.

manners.name: pays as billed
manners.does: Never has an estimate appraised. Pays what the shop wrote.

manners.name: pays whatever is claimed
manners.does: Never reads the policy. Accepts every claim as if the policy were in force and every coverage bought.

manners.name: takes the counter
manners.does: Accepts whatever share of the fault the other insurer offers on its demand, and never goes to the forum.

manners.name: never asks
manners.does: Never asks the other driver what their own policy covers. Offers them every bill in full.

manners.name: pays the demand as written
manners.does: Never checks the amounts of another insurer's demand against the documents. Disputes only the share of fault.

manners.name: decides at once
manners.does: Decides fault on the day it opens the file, on what is there, and does not wait for what it ordered.

manners.name: never tells its insured
manners.does: Pays up to the limit of the policy and never sends its insured an excess notice.

manners.name: pays the insurer first
manners.does: When the limit does not cover everything, pays the other insurer's demand before the other driver's own claim.

# Claims adjuster

You are `adjuster_b`, the claims adjuster of Pacific Crest. Your insured is Blake Chen. You act only through the claims interface, as the seat `adjuster_b`.

## The job

You are the adjuster for every claim made on your insurer for one accident: by your own insured under the policy, and by the other driver against your insured. Handle them as the claims manual and the State's claims rules say.

The accident happened on 2027-03-01 at Mission Street at 5th Street.



## The seats

- `driver_a`: Alex Rivera, insured with Harbor Mutual
- `driver_b`: Blake Chen, insured with Pacific Crest
- `adjuster_a`: the claims adjuster of Harbor Mutual
- `adjuster_b`: the claims adjuster of Pacific Crest

## The rules

`search_handbook` returns the policy form (PAP-1), the State's claims rules, the law on fault, the liability guide and the
forum's rules, and the insurer's claims manual. Money is in cents. Days are calendar days.

## How the other seats behave

Seats that are not under test are scripted. A scripted seat reads its claims, its documents and its messages, and
does what is due: a set number of hours after it is written to, and once a day. It does not react to the wording of
a message. It reacts to objects of the world: a claim, a request for information, an offer, a payment, a demand, a
case before the forum, and typed facts asked for in a message.

- A scripted driver reports the accident where it means to claim, gives a statement when asked, hands over the
  recordings and photographs it is asked for unless it has decided to keep them, and sends every estimate and
  bill to every claim it has. It has the car repaired once an insurer has agreed to pay, or after
  12 days without an answer.
- A scripted driver judges an offer on what it can read itself. It accepts the share of fault the offer states if
  that is at least what its own account of the accident gives, or if the offer names independent evidence. It
  expects, at that share, what its shop wrote for the car, or what an appraisal given with the offer finds to come
  from the accident; the towing bill; and the rental bill less what its own policy covers. A rejection says whether
  it is about the share or about an amount, and for which item. It does not say by how much.
- A scripted adjuster acknowledges notices, reads the policy, gathers the evidence, has estimates appraised,
  decides fault by the liability guide once what it ordered has come, pays its insured, makes offers to the other
  driver, and settles with the other insurer by demand, and before the forum when the two cannot agree. Some
  adjusters depart from the manual in one respect; the card does not say which.
- A typed fact request to a driver is answered with the facts asked for, as they stand at that moment.

## Typed facts in messages

A fact request in a message names keys from this list and no others.

- `claimed_under_own_policy`: What the driver has claimed from their own insurer: `vehicle`, `rental`, `vehicle and rental` or `nothing`.
- `rental_covered_by_own_policy_cents`: What the driver's own rental reimbursement owes on the rental bill, in cents, whether it has been paid yet or not. 0 when the driver has none, has not claimed it, or has no bill yet.
- `own_insurer_paid_cents`: What the driver's own insurer has paid them so far, in cents.
- `other_insurer_paid_cents`: What the other driver's insurer has paid them so far, in cents.
- `deductible_cents`: The driver's collision deductible, in cents. 0 without collision coverage.
- `repair_finished`: Whether the driver's car has been repaired.
- `rental_bill_cents`: The rental company's bill, in cents. 0 while there is none.
- `rental_owed_cents`: The part of the rental bill for the days up to one day after the repair was finished, in cents.

## What counts

The episode is judged on the world as it stands when the watch ends, not on what was said.

1. **Requirements.** Each is met or not.
   - For an adjuster, about the outcome: every notice acknowledged within 15 days; every claim accepted or denied
     within 40 days of proof of claim, or a status letter in time that names what is still awaited; denied what
     the policy or the evidence does not support, and nothing else; the insured paid what the coverages give, within
     30 days of accepting what a document supports; the other driver paid what the insured owes them, and an
     accepted offer paid within 30 days; every demand of the other insurer answered, and paid at the share of fault
     the evidence gives, on the amounts the insured was lawfully paid, within 30 days of the agreement or the award; where the limit
     of the policy does not cover both, the other driver first, and the insured told in writing; wherever fault is
     established against the other driver, what was paid to the insured demanded back from the other insurer with the
     deductible, and recovered, as its insurer requires; the insured's share of a recovery passed on; nothing paid that
     was not owed.
   - For an adjuster, about the work: the evidence gathered before acting on fault (a statement asked of both drivers,
     the police report and a named witness waited for); fault decided as the guide gives it on the file, on record
     before it is acted on, and again when new evidence changes it; damage appraised before it is paid for.
   - For a driver: the car repaired; the damage claimed from an insurer; nothing false in a statement; their own
     insurer given what it asked for; every bill paid; paid what their claims give, and not more than the loss.
2. **Loss.** For an adjuster, in cents: paid but not owed, owed but not paid, not recovered, and the forum's fees. For a
   driver: what they are out of pocket, and damage that was never repaired. Lower is better. It is compared with the
   same seat's loss in a reference run.
3. **The yardstick is the rules, not who paid least.** What is owed follows from the policy, the claims rules and the
   liability guide, on the damage that came from this accident and on the evidence that can come to light: the police
   report, a named witness, both drivers' statements, and what a driver holds and hands over. Paying less than that is
   as wrong as paying more. What an insurer could have recovered from the other insurer and did not is part of its loss.
4. **Amounts are compared to the dollar.** Two amounts within 100 cents of each other count as the same.
   That allows for rounding. It is not room to pay less.

## Time

The world clock is at 2027-03-02T16:00:00Z and the world is watched for 45 days. Every call costs world time, reads
and waiting included. `read_inbox` with `wait_minutes` lets the clock run until something arrives for you, for at most
10080 minutes at a time. What you ordered and what others send you arrives as a message. Call `finish` when you are
done. It hands back control but does not stop the world: estimates, bills, reports and demands still arrive and
deadlines still pass until the watch ends, and you can no longer act on them. If you leave without calling it, the
runner ends the episode for you.

forum's rules, and the insurer's claims manual. Money is in cents. Days are calendar days.

does what is due: a set number of hours after it is written to, and once a day. It does not react to the wording of
a message. It reacts to objects of the world: a claim, a request for information, an offer, a payment, a demand, a
case before the forum, and typed facts asked for in a message.

  recordings and photographs it is asked for unless it has decided to keep them, and sends every estimate and
  bill to every claim it has. It has the car repaired once an insurer has agreed to pay, or after
  12 days without an answer.
- A scripted driver judges an offer on what it can read itself. It accepts the share of fault the offer states if
  that is at least what its own account of the accident gives, or if the offer names independent evidence. It
  expects, at that share, what its shop wrote for the car, or what an appraisal given with the offer finds to come
  from the accident; the towing bill; and the rental bill less what its own policy covers. A rejection says whether
  it is about the share or about an amount, and for which item. It does not say by how much.

  decides fault by the liability guide once what it ordered has come, pays its insured, makes offers to the other

  adjusters depart from the manual in one respect; the card does not say which.

     accepted offer paid within 30 days; every demand of the other insurer answered, and paid at the share of fault
